key_insight: An incremental Deep Energy Method can model ductile fracture by coupling J2 plasticity and phase-field damage with separate neural representations for displacement and crack evolution.
engineering_relevance: This offers a mesh-free, physics-informed surrogate for predicting force response, plasticity, and crack growth in elasto-plastic solids with reduced reliance on conventional finite elements.
method: Alternating minimization of displacement and phase-field energies
ReZero residual network for displacement and localized Gaussian radial basis functions for phase field
Radial return updates for local plastic history with transfer learning across load steps
evidence_signal: The method was benchmarked against finite-element reference solutions and showed close agreement in force-displacement curves, energy evolution, plastic deformation, and crack propagation.
watch_item: Accuracy becomes more sensitive to the size of loading increments near sudden fracture events, so step control is important.
paper_title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
